status_legend.candidate: Lawful route that may fit, subject to facts and bank approval
status_legend.conditional: Lawful only if specific eligibility and documentary conditions are met
status_legend.limited: Lawful but capped at a size that cannot move the full balance
status_legend.prohibited: Unlawful or legally void; risk information only, no execution steps
status_legend.unverified: Plausible but no official rule or published price could be confirmed

_meta.disclaimer: No personal fact (account type, residency, source of funds, tax paid, receiving bank) is known. Status is a legal-eligibility screen, not advice or an approval.

routes.name: Bank purchase and wire of documented China current-account income (overseas individual)
routes.zh: 境外个人经常项目合法人民币收入购汇汇出
routes.one_line: If the RMB is lawful current-account income earned in China and you are an overseas individual, the bank may buy USD with it and remit abroad on documentary proof.
routes.who: Passport holder classified by the bank as an overseas individual (境外个人) under S01 Article 37.
steps: Ask the bank to confirm your account-holder classification (境内个人 vs 境外个人) and which article it will apply.
Assemble identity, the source-of-funds trail for each portion of the balance, and the China tax payment evidence (S03 requires a tax record or an explanation that the income is non-taxable).
Submit a purchase (购汇) application at the bank; the bank reviews authenticity and consistency of documents (S27 Article 12).
The bank converts RMB to USD at its prevailing rate and remits to your own overseas account; retain the purchase slip and remittance receipt.
Reconcile the receipt with U.S. income reporting, FBAR/8938 and any section 988 currency gain.
pros: No USD 50,000 annual purchase quota is published for overseas individuals (S05; S03).
Built on current-account convertibility (S27 Article 5; S01 Article 13).
Bank tariff is published and computable (S09).
cons: Bank discretion on documents is the binding constraint, not a published checklist.
Tax evidence is required in substance; unpaid China tax can block the purchase.
Only covers income that is genuinely current-account; savings or capital gains need another route.
limits: No published annual purchase cap for 境外个人
Single remittance identity checks above CNY 5,000 / USD 1,000 (S11)
routes.note: This is the only route in the catalog that combines published current-account convertibility with no published annual purchase cap.

routes.name: Employer payroll remittance of salary (overseas individual)
routes.zh: 境外个人工资薪金由单位代发汇出
routes.one_line: Some employers remit net salary abroad through a payroll partner; the bank still performs the individual purchase review.
routes.who: Current employee of a China entity with payroll remittance service.
steps: Confirm with payroll whether the employer remits abroad or only credits a China account.
Provide the payroll provider the same identity, tax and source documents the bank requires.
Check who bears the wire fee and at which rate the conversion is done; obtain the trade confirmation.
Keep the payroll statement, tax withholding record and remittance advice for U.S. reporting.
pros: Recurring and administratively simple if offered
Tax withholding record doubles as source evidence
cons: Not available to former employees or accumulated balances
Fee and FX markup are set by the employer's bank, often undisclosed to you
Payroll providers may refuse non-resident classifications
routes.note: Modeled on the published BOC tariff only; the actual payroll rail and its pricing are unknown.

routes.name: Convert back unused RMB within 24 months of the original exchange
routes.zh: 原兑换未用完人民币兑回
routes.one_line: RMB left over from a documented foreign-currency exchange can be converted back with the original slip for 24 months.
routes.who: Holder of the original exchange receipt (水单).
steps: Locate the original exchange slip (水单) showing the earlier FX-to-RMB conversion.
Present ID and the slip at the bank within 24 months of the exchange date.
For small same-day amounts (up to USD 500, or USD 1,000 at land-border departure points), ID alone is sufficient per S02 Article 13(2).
Retain the reversal slip for U.S. records.
pros: Explicit published rule with a 24-month window
No quota question for overseas individuals
cons: Capped by the original exchange amount
Requires a slip most people no longer hold
Expires
limits: USD 1,000/day at departure points without receipt
routes.note: Amounts beyond the original exchange are outside this route.

routes.name: Return unused inbound foreign currency by the original route
routes.zh: 境外个人未使用境外汇入外汇原路汇回
routes.one_line: Foreign currency wired in and not used can be sent back the same way with ID.
routes.who: Overseas individual with unused inbound FX still in the account.
steps: Identify the original inbound remittance and confirm the funds remain in the FX account.
Request the return remittance with ID; the bank matches it to the inbound record.
Confirm the return leg's fee schedule and rate with the bank before sending.
pros: No conversion purchase question if the funds are still in FX
cons: Applies to FX, not to RMB already held
Capped at the unused inbound amount
Return leg fees are charged again
routes.note: Useful only for funds that entered as foreign currency and were never converted.

routes.name: Domestic-individual annual facilitation quota (USD 50,000)
routes.zh: 境内个人年度便利化购汇额度5万美元
routes.one_line: If you are classified as a domestic individual, USD 50,000 per calendar year can be purchased with ID alone.
routes.who: Chinese citizen with a resident ID, or a foreigner holding a permanent-resident ID (S04).
steps: Confirm with the bank that you are classified as a domestic individual (or hold a permanent-resident ID).
Purchase within the USD 50,000 annual facilitation quota with ID.
Remit the purchased FX to your own overseas account; keep the purchase slip.
Repeat in later calendar years only if the quota is genuinely available to you; quotas cannot be carried over or borrowed.
pros: No documentary source review inside the quota
cons: Capped at USD 50,000 per person per calendar year (S02 Article 2)
Does not apply to plain overseas individuals (S05)
Using another person's quota is prohibited splitting (S01 Article 7)
limits: USD 50,000 per person per calendar year
routes.note: At USD 400,000 this route needs at least eight calendar years if nothing else applies.

routes.name: Domestic-individual purchase above quota with transaction documents
routes.zh: 境内个人超额度经常项目购汇
routes.one_line: Above the quota, a domestic individual can purchase FX for a genuine current-account purpose with supporting documents.
routes.who: Domestic individual with a documented current-account use (study, medical, travel, family support).
steps: Identify the permitted current-account purpose and the documents that evidence it.
Submit the purchase application with ID and the purpose documents; the bank reviews consistency.
Remit to the counterparty or your own account as the purpose requires.
Retain the full document set; the bank may re-check after the fact.
pros: No fixed cap if the purpose is genuine and documented
cons: Cannot be used to move savings without a qualifying purpose
Purpose must match the remittance
Bank may refuse
docs: Purpose documents (admission letter, medical invoice, etc.)
routes.note: This is not a route for relabeling a general savings balance.

routes.name: Permanent-resident ID holder using the facilitation quota
routes.zh: 持外国人永久居留身份证适用购汇额度
routes.one_line: An overseas individual holding a foreign permanent-resident ID may use the USD 50,000 purchase quota.
routes.who: Overseas individual with a valid 外国人永久居留身份证.
steps: Present the permanent-resident ID and passport.
Use the annual facilitation quota for purchase.
Reconcile the resulting remittance in U.S. reporting.
cons: Capped at USD 50,000 per year
Requires the PR ID
Does not convert capital-account balances
limits: USD 50,000 per person per calendar year
routes.note: A rare case where the quota is available to a non-citizen.

routes.name: Remit foreign currency already sitting in the FX savings account
routes.zh: 外汇储蓄账户内外汇直接汇出
routes.one_line: If part of the balance is already USD or another foreign currency, it can be remitted without any RMB conversion.
routes.who: Overseas individual with an FX savings account.
steps: Confirm the account is an FX savings account and the currency is actually held (not RMB).
Request the outward remittance with ID; overseas individuals can remit from an FX savings account with ID (S02 Article 15).
Pay commission and cable charges; no FX margin applies because no conversion occurs.
pros: ID-only documentary basis for the remittance leg
cons: Only works for the FX portion of the balance
Cash-based FX is harder than account-based FX
Receiving and intermediary fees still apply
routes.note: The cheapest rail per dollar when the balance is already in USD.

routes.name: Emigrant property transfer (pre-emigration assets)
routes.zh: 移民财产转移
routes.one_line: A person who emigrated from mainland China can transfer property owned before obtaining the immigration status, after SAFE approval.
routes.who: Natural person who moved from mainland China to a foreign country and owns lawful pre-emigration property.
steps: Confirm the assets were owned before the immigration status was obtained (S07 Article 2).
Apply to the SAFE branch at the original household-registration location with the application, identity, immigration proof and property-source documents.
Obtain the approval and 核准件, then take it to the designated bank.
The bank sells FX and remits directly to your own overseas account; cash withdrawal in China is not permitted (S07 Article 11).
No staged release is required after 汇发[2014]2号 (S06); the bank may remit once or in installments within the approved amount.
pros: No 500,000 CNY central filing threshold since 2014 (S06)
cons: SAFE approval required
Property must predate the immigration status
Notarisation and source documents still take time; approval is discretionary
routes.note: This is the main lawful route for a US citizen who emigrated with assets still in China.

routes.name: Inheritance property transfer
routes.zh: 继承财产转移
routes.one_line: A foreign citizen who lawfully inherited Chinese assets can remit the realised proceeds after SAFE approval.
routes.who: Foreign citizen or HK/Macau resident who inherited mainland assets.
steps: Obtain the inheritance documents (will, court judgment or notarised succession).
Apply to the SAFE branch where the deceased was registered, with identity, inheritance proof and the deceased's asset documents plus tax evidence.
After approval, take the 核准件 to the bank for purchase and remittance to your own overseas account.
Multiple decedents can now be combined in one application (S06).
cons: Requires completed succession, which can take years
Tax clearance for the deceased's assets is required
Approval is discretionary
routes.note: This is the only published capital-account route for a foreign heir.

routes.name: Sale of domestic property by an overseas individual
routes.zh: 境外个人出售境内商品房购汇汇出
routes.one_line: An overseas individual who sells self-use domestic property may remit the RMB proceeds after SAFE approval.
routes.who: Overseas individual who owned and sold domestic commercial housing.
steps: Complete the sale and pay the applicable China taxes (VAT and IIT; see the tax page).
Apply to SAFE for approval to purchase FX with the sale proceeds (S01 Article 22).
Take the approval to the bank; proceeds must go to your own overseas account.
Retain the sale contract, tax receipts and approval for U.S. reporting.
pros: Explicit legal basis in S01 Article 22
cons: SAFE approval required
China IIT 20% on the gain (or 1% deemed) applies
Property must have been self-use and lawfully held
routes.note: Tax is on the property gain, not on the conversion.

routes.name: Domestic individual selling property and remitting proceeds
routes.zh: 境内个人出售房产后购汇汇出
routes.one_line: A domestic individual selling property faces the capital-account rules and cannot simply wire the proceeds abroad.
routes.who: Chinese citizen with resident ID selling domestic property.
steps: Settle the property taxes and obtain the tax receipts.
Determine whether an emigrant-transfer or other capital-account approval applies; a plain sale does not create a right to remit.
If approved, purchase FX at the bank and remit to your own overseas account.
pros: Possible if an emigration or other approved basis exists
cons: Domestic individuals cannot freely remit property proceeds
Approval depends on a qualifying capital-account basis
20% IIT on the gain
routes.note: Flagged because many online guides present a domestic property sale as a simple remittance route; it is not.

routes.name: Foreign-invested enterprise dividend to a foreign individual shareholder
routes.zh: 外商投资企业向外籍个人股东分配股息
routes.one_line: Genuine FIE profits can be distributed, but from 1 September 2026 the 20% dividend rate applies to foreign individuals.
routes.who: Foreign individual shareholder of a China FIE with distributable profits.
steps: Confirm the company has audited distributable profits and a board resolution.
Withholding is due at 20% under 2026 No. 27 (S16); treaty relief, if any, must be analysed separately.
The company withholds and the bank remits the net dividend against the resolution and tax filing.
Report the gross dividend and the Chinese tax on your U.S. return; claim a foreign tax credit where allowed.
pros: Withholding is handled by the company
Treaty may cap China tax at 10% in some cases (unverified for your facts)
cons: 20% China tax since 2026-09-01 (the old exemption is repealed)
Requires real profits and corporate formalities
Treaty relief is fact-specific
routes.note: This route is not available for personal savings disguised as a dividend.

routes.name: Equity transfer proceeds
routes.zh: 股权转让所得汇出
routes.one_line: Proceeds from a genuine equity transfer can be remitted after China tax and registration steps.
routes.who: Foreign individual transferring equity in a China company.
steps: Complete the equity transfer and the market-supervision registration.
Pay 20% IIT on the transfer gain as asset-transfer income (S15 Article 3).
Take the transfer documents, tax receipt and registration to the bank for remittance.
cons: Valuation disputes are common
Tax must be settled first
Bank documentary review
routes.note: Assumes a genuine arm's-length transfer.

routes.name: Liquidation proceeds of a foreign-invested enterprise
routes.zh: 外商投资企业清算所得汇出
routes.one_line: After lawful liquidation and tax, the foreign investor's RMB share may be purchased and remitted.
routes.who: Foreign investor in a liquidated FIE.
steps: Complete liquidation, tax clearance and deregistration.
Present the liquidation and tax documents to the bank for purchase and remittance.
Retain the distribution computation for U.S. reporting.
cons: Slow and expensive process
Tax clearance first
Only for genuine equity
routes.note: A business exit, not a personal-transfer workaround.

routes.name: B-share sale proceeds
routes.zh: 境外个人B股交易所得
routes.one_line: Overseas individuals may hold B shares; sale proceeds follow securities and FX rules.
routes.who: Overseas individual with a B-share account.
steps: Sell through the licensed securities company.
Follow the broker's and bank's FX settlement procedure for the proceeds.
Report the gain on your U.S. return.
pros: Explicitly permitted for overseas individuals (S01 Article 23)
cons: Only applies to B-share holdings
Securities and FX procedures apply
Market risk
limits: Sale proceeds of existing holdings only
routes.note: No published bank tariff specific to B-share settlement was located; costs are UNVERIFIED.

routes.name: Bank counter or e-banking telegraphic transfer (BOC published tariff)
routes.zh: 银行柜面/电子银行电汇
routes.one_line: The execution rail for most lawful routes: BOC publishes 0.1% commission (min CNY 50, max CNY 260) plus CNY 150 cable outside HK/Macau/Taiwan.
routes.who: Anyone with an approved purchase or FX balance.
steps: Obtain the purchase approval or FX balance.
Submit the remittance with the beneficiary's own-name account details.
Pay commission plus cable charge at the published schedule; confirm any local discount or surcharge.
Keep the remittance advice; allow for intermediary and receiving-bank deductions.
cons: Intermediary and receiving bank fees are not published by BOC
Local pricing can differ (note 1 of S09)
Rate is set at execution, not at quote
routes.note: This is the backbone cost model used for every bank-based route on this site.

routes.name: Other Chinese bank tariffs (ICBC, CCB, ABC, CMB, HSBC China)
routes.zh: 其他中资银行个人跨境汇款费率
routes.one_line: Other banks publish their own tariffs, but no current mainland personal schedule was verified in this session.
routes.who: Account holders at those banks.
steps: Ask the branch for its current published personal cross-border remittance schedule in writing.
Compare total cost for the same USD outcome at the same time, including FX rate and all fees.
Do not rely on this site for another bank's price; it was not verified.
pros: Competition may produce lower local pricing
cons: No verified schedule here
Prices vary by branch and channel
Comparison must be same-time to be meaningful
routes.note: Deliberately left unquantified rather than estimated.

routes.name: Wise transfer from CNY
routes.zh: Wise 人民币汇出
routes.one_line: Wise supports sending from CNY only for eligible workers or former workers with China tax records, to an account you own abroad.
routes.who: Non-mainland-Chinese person who worked in China and has a China tax record showing tax paid in the last three years.
steps: Confirm eligibility: work history in China and a qualifying tax record (S26).
Complete Wise verification (typically 1-2 working days).
Send from the China bank app (max CNY 300,000 per transfer) or Alipay (max CNY 50,000) to your own overseas account.
Check the live fee and rate in the quote before confirming; retain the receipt.
pros: Transparent mid-market rate in the quote
No need to visit a branch
Uses a licensed China payment partner
cons: Eligibility excludes people without China work/tax history
Overall limit is based on after-tax salary, not the account balance
Fee is dynamic and not published as a schedule
limits: Overall limit tied to documented after-tax income
routes.note: A rail, not a legal basis: the underlying funds still need a lawful source. The fee was not quantified because it is quote-based.

routes.name: Alipay / WeChat cross-border remittance for mainland residents
routes.zh: 支付宝/微信跨境汇款（境内居民）
routes.one_line: Payment apps offer remittance to mainland residents under their own limits; availability to an overseas individual was not verified.
routes.who: Mainland resident users, subject to each app's rules.
steps: Check the app's own eligibility and limits; no official rule confirming access for a non-resident was located.
Compare the all-in cost, including the app's FX markup, against a bank wire.
Retain the receipt.
cons: Eligibility unclear for this user
FX markup is the real cost and is not published as a rate
Limits are low
routes.note: Flagged: no official confirmation of access for an overseas individual.

routes.name: Spend RMB directly abroad with a UnionPay card
routes.zh: 银联卡境外消费
routes.one_line: Card spending abroad uses RMB without a purchase-quota charge, but it is spending, not a transfer of the balance.
routes.who: Holder of a mainland-issued UnionPay card.
steps: Use the card for genuine purchases abroad.
The issuer converts at its card rate; no separate purchase application is made.
Check the statement for the applied rate and any foreign-transaction fee.
pros: Does not consume the USD 50,000 purchase quota (S13)
cons: Cannot convert the balance into USD cash
FX markup is set by the issuer and not published here
Merchant acceptance limits use
routes.note: A consumption tool, not a repatriation route.

routes.name: Withdraw RMB cash abroad at an ATM
routes.zh: 境外ATM提取人民币现钞
routes.one_line: ATMs abroad dispense local currency within a CNY 10,000/day and CNY 100,000/year per-person cap.
routes.who: Holder of a mainland-issued bank card.
steps: Withdraw at an overseas ATM within the daily and annual caps (S13).
Compare the issuer's conversion rate and ATM operator fee.
Track the annual total; exceeding it suspends overseas cash access for the current and following year (S13).
cons: CNY 100,000/year cap makes USD 400,000 impossible (about 4 years at the cap)
ATM and issuer fees are not published here
Cash handling risk
limits: CNY 100,000 per person per calendar year
routes.note: Cap converted for display only at the BOC board rate; the rule is stated in CNY, not USD.

routes.name: Carry foreign-currency cash out
routes.zh: 携带外币现钞出境
routes.one_line: Cash carriage is capped at USD 5,000 without a permit and USD 10,000 with a bank carriage certificate.
routes.who: Traveller departing China.
steps: Purchase the foreign currency lawfully first; cash uses the bank's cash rate.
Up to USD 5,000 equivalent normally needs no carriage permit (S14).
From USD 5,000 to USD 10,000, obtain a 携带外汇出境许可证 from the designated bank (S14).
Above USD 10,000 the permit must come from SAFE, and carrying more than USD 10,000 is exceptional (S14).
Do not split trips or use other travellers to evade the limit (S01 Article 7; S27 Article 42).
cons: Cannot move USD 400,000 lawfully: 80 trips at the USD 5,000 threshold
Physical and theft risk
Excess carriage is punishable (S27 Article 42)
limits: USD 5,000 per trip normally without a permit
USD 5,000-10,000 needs a bank-issued carriage permit
Above USD 10,000 needs a SAFE-issued permit and is exceptional
routes.note: For USD 400,000 this is 80 trips at the no-permit threshold: not a practical route. Thresholds verified against SAFE, not against a customs page.

routes.name: RMB wire to an offshore RMB account (CNH)
routes.zh: 人民币跨境汇至境外人民币账户
routes.one_line: Sending RMB itself to an offshore account may be possible for some current-account purposes, but no rule confirming access for this user was verified.
routes.who: Holder of an offshore RMB account and a qualifying current-account purpose.
steps: Ask the bank whether it will process an individual cross-border RMB remittance for your purpose and to your jurisdiction.
Obtain the receiving bank's confirmation that it accepts RMB.
Price the conversion at the offshore end separately.
cons: No verified individual rule
US banks rarely accept RMB
Offshore conversion has its own spread
routes.note: Flagged as unverified rather than recommended.

routes.name: Hold RMB and convert later, or spend it on future China trips
routes.zh: 保留人民币，择机兑换或未来消费
routes.one_line: Doing nothing is a real option: no fee is paid, but you keep currency and policy risk.
routes.who: Anyone not forced to convert now.
steps: Estimate near-term RMB needs for travel, family or China expenses.
Keep that portion in RMB; convert the rest when a lawful route and a favourable rate exist.
Review annually; rules and rates change.
pros: Useful if you still spend in China
cons: FX exposure is unhedged
Policy can tighten
Inflation and opportunity cost
routes.note: The only route with a verified zero fee, because nothing is converted.

routes.name: Crypto / USDT OTC conversion and transfer
routes.zh: 虚拟货币/USDT场外兑换
routes.one_line: Converting RMB to crypto in China is prohibited; the 2026 notice treats fiat-crypto exchange as illegal financial activity.
routes.who: Not lawful.
cons: Fiat-to-crypto conversion in China is prohibited (S12).
Financial institutions may not provide accounts or settlement for it (S12).
No legal recourse if the counterparty disappears.
U.S. tax and FBAR obligations still apply to any offshore account.
routes.note: Risk information only. No execution steps are provided.

routes.name: Underground bank / private currency broker (地下钱庄)
routes.zh: 地下钱庄
routes.one_line: Private cross-border settlement is illegal and exposed to confiscation and criminal liability.
routes.who: Not lawful.
cons: Illegal trading of foreign exchange carries confiscation and fines up to 30% (or 30%-100% if serious) under S27 Article 45.
Funds can be seized or lost entirely.
U.S. reporting duties are unaffected.
routes.note: Risk information only.

routes.name: Splitting the balance across friends' or family quotas
routes.zh: 分拆结售汇（借用他人额度）
routes.one_line: Using other people's quotas or splitting transactions to evade limits is expressly prohibited.
routes.who: Not lawful.
cons: S01 Article 7 prohibits splitting to evade limit supervision.
Participants can be placed on a watch list and lose quota access.
Funds can be frozen during investigation.
routes.note: Risk information only.

routes.name: False trade or service invoices (misinvoicing)
routes.zh: 虚假贸易/服务单证
routes.one_line: Fabricated commercial documents to obtain FX are illegal, even if a real good or service exists elsewhere.
routes.who: Not lawful.
cons: S01 Article 7 prohibits false commercial documents to evade authenticity review.
Illegal FX purchase under S27 Article 40 carries fines up to 30% (or 30%-100%) plus repatriation orders.
Criminal exposure in serious cases.
routes.note: Risk information only.

routes.name: Buying overseas property or investment insurance with purchased FX
routes.zh: 购汇用于境外买房或投资性保险
routes.one_line: Overseas property and securities investment are capital-account uses that are not open to individual purchase.
routes.who: Not lawful without approval.
cons: Capital-account FX payments require approval (S27 Article 22; S01 Articles 16-17, 20).
Overseas individuals are separately barred from most domestic financial products (S01 Article 23) — the mirror logic applies outward.
Mis-describing the purpose is a false-declaration risk.
routes.note: The specific prohibited-use list in the 个人购汇申请书 was not retrieved verbatim in this session and is flagged.

routes.name: Export gold or precious metals to bypass FX rules
routes.zh: 出口黄金或贵金属规避外汇管理
routes.one_line: Gold export is subject to separate restrictions, but the exact personal limit was not verified here.
routes.who: Not established as lawful.
cons: Precious-metal export is separately regulated; no official personal allowance was confirmed in this session.
Carrying or shipping metal to realise value abroad raises customs and AML issues (S11).
Any gain is still taxable in the U.S.
routes.note: Flagged as unverified; not presented as a route.

routes.name: Gift the RMB to a relative abroad to avoid approval
routes.zh: 以赠与境外亲属方式转移
routes.one_line: Outward gifts of capital require approval; calling a transfer a gift does not remove the requirement.
routes.who: Only with SAFE approval under the capital-account rules.
cons: S01 Article 20 requires approval for outward donations and property transfers.
Relabeling a capital transfer as a gift is a false declaration.
On the U.S. side, a foreign gift over USD 100,000 triggers Form 3520 reporting (S29), though not income tax.
routes.note: Included to correct a common misconception; no approval-free gift route was found.
